hook: ONE HIDDEN CRACK.|THE WHOLE BRIDGE FELL.
photo_credit: Photo: the Silver Bridge, Point Pleasant, W.Va. (Digital Public Library of America, via Wikimedia Commons) — no known restrictions

scenes.say: December 15, 1967. The Silver Bridge over the Ohio River collapses, with thirty-seven vehicles on it.

One joint held its north chain together: a pin through the eyes of two steel eyebars. At that pin, a crack had grown for forty years, to about an eighth of an inch. Then the eye broke, and its sister bar slid off the pin.
No inspection could have found it: it was hidden inside the joint. And each link had only two bars. With three or more, one break might not have dropped the chain. With two, it was inevitable.
Forty-six people died. Thirty-one of the thirty-seven vehicles on the bridge fell with it.

comment: No inspection of the time could have found that crack. What should a design do about a part nobody can inspect?
